applicability: Any dense detail pass, market/street scene, machinery district, interior set, rooftop kitbash, ruin courtyard, or social-media showcase build.
core_rule: Detail must be grouped into authored design units with purpose and hierarchy. Density alone is not design.
hierarchy: authored modules such as shop, kiosk, maintenance node, planter cluster, service bay, shrine, lab bench, food stall
secondary props tied to those modules
final accent clutter only where it supports the scene
anti_patterns: even random scatter across all available floor space
pipes or crates blocking pedestrian lanes without design reason
unclustered lamps/screens/props with no readable function
decorations placed only to raise density
repeating a shop/stall module without identity changes
validation_questions: Can the player identify the main path?
Does each prop cluster have a role?
Are there breathing spaces between dense zones?
Is the detail tied to a wall, storefront, counter, garden, machine bay, or route?
Would removing 30% of loose props improve the read?
